prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Welcome Back to Your Desktop Pet", "Sign in to instantly restore your pets, custom traits, and saved items across your devices."]
1: ["Official Adoption Verified"]
2: []
3: ["Your pet will anchor to the bottom-right corner of your desktop taskbar once setup completes."]
4: ["How to Interact with Your Pet", "Learn how to control and summon your desktop companion at any time.", "Right click pet for menu; Drag to move across monitors; Double click to speak"]
5: []
6: ["Custom Pet Creation Guide", "Follow these guidelines for optimal custom pet generation results.", "Use clear front-facing lighting; Ensure subject is centered; Avoid blurry backgrounds"]
7: ["Pro tip: Hover over your pet to check stats or press Alt+P to summon it anywhere on screen."]
8: ["Sync Your Companion Across Desktops", "Connect your account to keep your pet's personality, accessories, and memory safe on any PC."]
9: ["Your Pet Has Arrived!", "Your new companion is ready to hang out on your desktop background."]
